chunks: And he (peace be upon him) said:
Adhere to contracts and entrust their fulfilment to steadfast persons.

key_terms.أَوْتَادِهَا: Its stakes (metaphor for firmness and steadfastness in fulfillment)
key_terms.الذِّمَمِ: Covenants, contracts, or pledges of trust

ai.seo_question: What does it mean to adhere to contracts in Shia ethics?
ai.summary: In this concise rhetorical style characteristic of Nahj al-Balagha, Imam Ali (AS) employs the metaphor of 'stakes' (awtād) to emphasize that covenants must be anchored with the same stability and immovability as the foundational pegs of a tent. This instruction underscores the theological weight of *al-dhimmah* (the pledge of faith/contract) in Shia jurisprudence, where fulfilling obligations to God and people is a primary marker of piety and social integrity.

en.sayed-ali-raza: 155. Amīr al-mu’minīn, peace be upon him, said:
Adhere to contracts and entrust their fulfilment to steadfast persons.
